rationale: Localized argument-validation defect in one syscall entry file, not a missing subsystem. getsockopt is fully wired (kernel/src/syscall/getsockopt.rs, dispatched at arch/x86.rs) and the option tables it needs already exist, so this is unlike round 3's times03 (no handler at all). The test is 9 pure errno assertions with no filesystem or scheduling dependency, and every arm it exercises has an implementation to correct. The defect is concentrated in validation ORDER and errno CHOICE inside sys_getsockopt: (1) line 20 resolves the level BEFORE the fd, and maps an unknown level to EOPNOTSUPP, so tcase 1 (fd 400, valid SOL_SOCKET) can only reach EBADF if the fd is resolved first, while tcase 5 (level 500) needs EOPNOTSUPP -- Linux resolves the socket first, then the level; (2) line 23 reads *optlen before the fd is resolved, so tcase 1's EBADF and tcase 2's ENOTSOCK are reachable only after moving the fd lookup above the optlen read, and tcase 4 (optlen=NULL) must still yield EFAULT from that same read; (3) SOL_UDP is a declared CSocketOptionLevel variant (options/mod.rs:190) but new_raw_socket_option has no arm for it, falling to the catch-all EOPNOTSUPP at line 174, which is what tcase 6 wants -- so that arm is already right and must not be 'fixed'; (4) tcases 7/8 want ENOPROTOOPT for optname -1 under IPPROTO_IP/IPPROTO_TCP, and new_ip_option / new_tcp_option already return exactly ENOPROTOOPT (ip.rs:74, tcp.rs:60), so those pass once the fd and level are resolved in the right order; (5) tcase 9 wants EINVAL for optlen=(socklen_t)-1, and no bound check on optlen exists anywhere in getsockopt.rs or setsockopt.rs, so that is the one genuinely additive piece. That makes the expected shape a reorder of three existing statements plus one new optlen bound check, all inside a 47-line file, with the option-table errnos already correct. Two prior committed runs (timerfd_gettime01, timer_gettime01) diagnosed this same 'hand-rolled guard runs before the fd is resolved' antipattern in other syscall entries and fixed it by reordering, which is direct evidence that this class of defect is small and self-contained here. Cache says host=pass on the pinned 20260529 prebuilt and probe=fail at exactly my base_commit e8f2b9ca6, so no host run and no re-probe were needed and neither observation is stale. Chose it over the 63 untaken stale-entry candidates because those are pool-edit-only and exercise no kernel defect; over statfs03/utime06 (both hinge on the unprivileged-EACCES path where DAC_OVERRIDE and set_euid capability handling are involved, a broader credentials story); over socketpair01 (its EPROTONOSUPPORT/EOPNOTSUPP arms are the socket01 defect already committed on fix-ltp-socket01-STzXZ3, which rewrote socketpair.rs, so it may already be green or would collide); over setitimer01 (needs real ITIMER_VIRTUAL/ITIMER_PROF signal delivery timing, not an errno fix); over pipe2_04 (needs F_SETPIPE_SZ/F_GETPIPE_SZ, absent from the FcntlCmd enum entirely); over prctl10 (PR_SET_TSC/PR_GET_TSC plus SIGSEGV-on-rdtsc, a hardware-flag feature); and over mincore/splice/tee/mlock/clock_settime candidates, all of which have no handler in arch/x86.rs at all and would repeat round 3's missing-feature outcome.
notes: all.txt line 564 is '# getsockopt01'; enable by removing the '# ' prefix. Default configuration -- pool is all.txt, so no CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR override and no extra blocklist, hence run_vars is empty. getsockopt02 sits on line 565 and stays commented; it is a separate cache stale-entry (observed passing at e8f2b9ca6 by run-ifrhdN) and is out of scope for this run. Round-4 coverage check: 29 sibling runs exist, 27 committed, 1 abandoned (times03, missing-feature), 1 in-progress/live (this run). getsockopt01 is taken by none of them and no fix-* branch touches getsockopt.rs. Appended nothing to select.cache: I ran no host binaries and booted no kernel, because the cache already held host=pass (pinned version 20260529) and probe=fail at my exact base_commit e8f2b9ca6 for every shortlist candidate. Per the phase rules an unmeasured test has nothing to record, so re-emitting another run's observations as my own would be guessing. Trap for diagnose: do NOT delete the SOL_UDP catch-all behaviour or change ip/tcp ENOPROTOOPT, both already match Linux; and tcase 3 (optval=NULL, valid optlen) expects EFAULT, which must come from write_to_user at line 38 rather than an early guard, so avoid adding a NULL check on optval.
